products.quality: Three explicit Start From modes (Absolute Coords, Current Position, User Origin) plus a 9-dot Job Origin anchor selector; the roster's most complete positioning model.
CNC work/machine coordinate model; project origin chosen from four corners or center, Z-zero top/bottom, set by jogging+Zero or Probing Wizard. No LightBurn-style current/user-origin toggle.
Basic GRBL zeroing—set work zero at current head position, homing/unlock buttons, jog panel for positioning. No absolute/user-origin mode selector.
Manual positioning by moving the laser module and recording vertices; real-time coordinate readout on canvas; homed machines use absolute bed placement.
Work Zero vs Home distinction; carve wizard sets work zero (toolpaths start at material's lower-left corner); homing switches establish machine home.
Per-axis or combined zeroing, Go-To zero buttons, probing to set zero, plus work coordinate systems—solid grbl/grblHAL origin handling.
Pause/Resume plus Ctrl+Break stop; resume works but GRBL feed-hold resume behavior is firmware-dependent and community threads report occasionally imperfect restarts.
Pause key pauses, Resume continues, Ctrl+Break stops; pause/abort issued as feed-hold to the CNC controller.
Feed-hold and Resume buttons issue grbl pause/resume; functional but no documented position-hold guarantees.
Processing pauses automatically on flame detection or device move/tilt (hardware-driven); explicit user pause/resume of an active job is thinly documented.
Pause/Resume in the carve panel; X-Carve Pro raises to safety height, stops spindle, then resumes at the same location—though some community reports note spindle not restarting on resume.
Clear model—Pause resumes from where you left off, Stop cancels completely; documented job-control basics.
Stop 'immediately aborts a currently running job'; Ctrl+Break keyboard shortcut also stops.
Stop sends an abort command to the controller; docs stress a physical E-stop must not be MillMage's only stop method.
Soft-reset/stop button halts grbl and resets the controller; combined with feed-hold for interruption.
Opening the enclosure stops the laser (interlock); device button and lid abort processing. Stop safe and hardware-backed.
Cancel button aborts the carve from the panel; spindle stops and bit raises.
Stop cancels the job completely and distinctly from Pause; documented clearly.
No automatic recovery, but Preview 'Start Here' scrubs the time slider to resume partway through—an officially documented, community-endorsed manual workaround for power-loss/disconnect.
Stopped jobs recoverable via 'Start Here' in the Preview window—manual resume-from-point, mirroring LightBurn's approach.
No built-in resume; strong community consensus it's impossible to continue an interrupted job—only manual G-code editing or a full restart.
No resume-after-failure/start-from-line found in XCS docs; interrupted jobs restart. Move/flame events pause but do not recover position.
No reliable resume-from-line; official 'restart after power loss' guidance plus community reports confirm you effectively re-home, re-zero and re-carve.

'Start from Line' is purpose-built for power-loss/USB-disconnect/overnight recovery; replays prior state (accessories, spindle/laser power, macros) up to the chosen line—the roster's strongest recovery.
Framing (bounding-box and rubber-band) plus out-of-bounds warnings ('Cut might be out of bounds', 'frame exceeds bounds of machine') surface config/position problems before running.
Framing (bounding-box/rubber-band/continuous) and a wireframe Preview to catch problems before starting; no documented soft-limit/bounds warning.
No built-in preflight or soft-limit/bounds validation documented; can command the head out of bounds. Perimeter checks only via user-defined custom-button macros.
Framing walks the border pre-job; Preview shows the toolpath and estimated time; enclosure/lid must be closed to start—positioning verified before processing.
Carve wizard checklist—confirm material secure, confirm bit size, set work zero—before spindle start; toolpath simulation and soft-limit pausing guard travel.
Strong preflight—G-code warnings flag suspect lines on load, a Soft-Limits warning flags files that may exceed the work area, plus Outline traces the job perimeter.
Busy status shows streaming progress with time; console surfaces machine status and decoded alarms. Current-line visibility via console rather than a headline counter.
Busy-state progress bar shows percentage of commands streamed with elapsed time and an estimate of remaining streaming time.
Filename + progress display, line counter, live time projection from actual speed, machine status/alarm readout, and a moving laser-position marker on canvas.
Preview shows estimated time and a scrubbable progress bar; live real-processing progress/current-line telemetry is limited in documentation.
Carve panel shows job progress while carving; Easel provides time estimates for toolpaths.
Fullest in-run telemetry—animated progress bar with completion %, estimated time remaining, g-code line counter and running timer, plus grbl alarm/error codes decoded to plain language.
'Cut Selected Graphics' toggle runs only selected objects, with optional 'Use Selection Origin'; Preview 'Start Here' also runs from an arbitrary point—the most complete run-subset control.
'Start Here' in the Preview window runs the job from a chosen point (run-from-here); object-level cut-selected not documented.
Runs the whole loaded G-code file only; no run-selected or run-from-here (resume from a line is impossible per community).
Per-object Output toggle—disabled objects aren't framed, previewed or processed—effectively runs only the enabled/selected objects.
Carves the entire design; no documented run-selected-only or mid-file run-from-here.
'Start from Line' runs from any chosen g-code line (run-from-here); no object-level cut-selected since gSender is a sender, not a CAM tool.
Software-side posture—framing, out-of-bounds warnings, safety docs—but no hardware interlock (drives third-party machines), so fire safety relies on the user and hardware.
Prominent in-app warnings—CNC can cause severe injury, never leave a running machine unattended, always have a physical E-stop, software stop must not be the sole method.
Thin posture—homing/alarm handling present, but no documented interlock awareness or fire-risk guidance; safety left to the user and hardware.
Strongest hardware safety—flame/spark detection pauses and alarms, tilt/move detection stops the job, enclosure-open interlock stops the laser, plus LSO safety-training gating.
Wizard enforces bit/material/work-zero confirmation and raises to safety height; soft-limit pausing; router+vacuum-on reminders. CNC injury risk handled procedurally, no software interlock.
Safety-conscious sender—reminds router+vacuum on before Start, Soft-Limits/G-code warnings, homing/limits support, decoded alarm codes; no hardware interlock (third-party CNCs).
